episodes.187813: Elevated thunderstorms produced many positive cloud-to-ground lightning strikes. One lightning strike caused significant damage in Montgomery County.
episodes.187951: Strong thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 22nd, as an upper level disturbance translated into the Southern Plains. The strongest storms produced hail up to penny size in Washington and Osage Counties.
episodes.188047: An unseasonably warm and humid airmass characterized by high temperatures in the upper 50s and lower 60s during the afternoon of February 21st preceded the approach of a cold front.  As the front sagged into central Illinois and a nocturnal low-level jet interacted with the boundary, scattered thunderstorms developed across north-central Illinois during the pre-dawn hours of February 22nd.  The strongest and longest lasting cell tracked from southern Knox County eastward into northern McLean County, producing hail as large as half dollars at times.
episodes.188714: Severe thunderstorms on February 22, 2024 brought damaging winds to central Arkansas.
episodes.188950: A cold frontal passage made its way through the Quad State region during the afternoon on the 22nd. MUCAPE was limited to around 500 J/kg with 0-3 km helicity at 100-200 m2/s2 in SE Missouri and adjacent portions of S Illinois, with less favorable conditions further east. The frontal boundary became a focus for a line of thunderstorms, with mid-level lapse rates and shear robust enough to produce hail, with marginally severe hail reported out of Anna, IL.
episodes.188951: A cold frontal passage made its way through the Quad State region during the afternoon on the 22nd. MUCAPE was limited to around 500 J/kg with 0-3 km helicity at 100-200 m2/s2. The frontal boundary became a focus for a line of thunderstorms, with mid-level lapse rates and shear robust enough to produce hail, with marginally severe hail reported in Bollinger and Cape Girardeau counties.
episodes.189331: A winter storm mid-February brought several days of continued heavy snow, rain, and gusty winds. Periods of chain controls were observed in the mountains with local reports of flooding and minor wind damage.

events.narrative: At approximately 9:00 AM PST on Thursday, February, 22, 2024, Shasta County Sheriff's Office responded to a report that rocks and debris had broken away from a hillside, near a drainage culvert that leads to the Sacramento River. Two juveniles were caught in the debris, fell down the hillside and died. Heavy rainfall impacted the area from February 18-21, 2024, with observed rainfall totals of 3-8 inches near the site of the incident.
The hail came from a storm embedded in a line moving southeastward through SE Missouri.
The storm that moved through north of Patton cycled and produced quarter size hail in Scopus as well.
Media relayed a report of nickel size hail covering the ground in Anna, with a delayed report of 1 inch hail.
Media relayed multiple reports of hail from a storm tracking southeastward through Cape Girardeau County. 1 inch hail was reported SW of Jackson and SSW of Cape Girardeau.
A lightning strike caused an electrical surge and significant damage in the basement of a house in the 21600 block of Gentry Lane.
Powerlines were blown down in East End.
